+name: Glossary Terms
+
+# cycle-128 FR-6 (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, D-6.3): every backticked framework
+# term in the kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) resolves to an entry or alias in
+# the framework glossary (.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md), or to an allowlisted code
+# identifier (.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt, at most 30 entries).
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh is the gate; the two control steps prove the
+# gate itself still bites. This check is Loa's own: it runs in this repository
+# only, never in a project that mounts the framework.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+
+jobs:
+  glossary-terms:
+    name: Kernel terms resolve to the glossary
+    if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
+        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
+
+      - name: Check kernel terms against the glossary
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file GLOSSARY.md
+
+      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the miss fixture with exit 1)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/miss
+          rc=0
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt" || rc=$?
+          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh did not reject $d with exit 1 (got $rc)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: miss fixture rejected"
+
+      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the ok fixture)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/ok
+          if ! bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt"; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh false-positive on $d"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: ok fixture accepted"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-validator.bats
+#
+# validate-artifact.sh --type glossary (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.4, §4.5): an
+# H1, a context paragraph before '## Language', one-line '**Term**: definition'
+# entries of at most two sentences and 300 characters, _Avoid_: and _Aliases_:
+# only directly below an entry, no duplicate term or alias, WARN on a path or
+# file extension in '## Language'. Cases write temp files only.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+    G="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/GLOSSARY.md"
+}
+
+# glossary <language-section lines...>: a valid head plus the given body
+glossary() {
+    { printf '# Glossary: test\n\nThe vocabulary of a test project.\n\n## Language\n\n'; printf '%s\n' "$@"; } > "$G"
+}
+
+val() { run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$G" "$@"; }
+
+@test "GV-1 the framework glossary validates with no warning" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-2 the root project glossary validates with no warning" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-3 both fixture glossaries validate" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary/ok/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary/miss/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-4 a well-formed entry with _Avoid_ and _Aliases_ lines passes" {
+    glossary '**Dissent**: A second review. It is triaged.' '_Avoid_: second opinion' '_Aliases_: DIS, counter-review' '' '### Group' '' '**Voice**: Who decided.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-5 a duplicate term fails, case-insensitively" {
+    glossary '**Spike**: A prototype.' '' '**spike**: Another one.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'term "spike" duplicates term "Spike"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-6 an alias that repeats a term or another alias fails" {
+    glossary '**Run mode**: Unattended runs.' '_Aliases_: RUNNING' '' '**Halt**: A stop.' '_Aliases_: running, run_mode'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'alias "running" duplicates alias "RUNNING"'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'alias "run_mode" duplicates term "Run mode"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-7 a definition over 300 characters fails" {
+    glossary "**Long**: $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 1 301))."
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'the definition of "Long" is 302 characters, over 300'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-8 a definition of exactly 300 characters passes; multibyte characters count once" {
+    glossary "**Edge**: $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 1 299))." "**Wide**: $(printf 'é%.0s' $(seq 1 299))."
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-9 a three-sentence definition fails; two sentences pass" {
+    glossary '**Three**: One. Two! Three?'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'the definition of "Three" has 3 sentences; at most two'* ]]
+    glossary '**Two**: One sentence here. And a second (with a note).'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-10 _Aliases_ without an entry fails" {
+    glossary '_Aliases_: orphan' '' '**Real**: An entry.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: is not directly after an entry"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-11 _Avoid_ separated from its entry by a blank line fails" {
+    glossary '**Real**: An entry.' '' '_Avoid_: other word'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Avoid_: is not directly after an entry"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-12 a missing ## Language section fails" {
+    printf '# Glossary: test\n\nContext.\n\n## Terms\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'no "## Language" section'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-13 a missing H1 or context paragraph fails" {
+    printf 'Context.\n\n## Language\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no H1"* ]]
+    printf '# Glossary: test\n\n## Language\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no context paragraph"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-14 a definition wrapped onto a second line fails" {
+    glossary '**Wrapped**: A definition that' 'continues on the next line.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"not an entry"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-15 a path or file extension in a definition WARNs and still passes" {
+    glossary '**Hook**: The guard in hooks/implement-gate that asks first.' '**Doc**: The plan in a markdown file named plan.md for review.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *":7: a path or file extension"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *":8: a path or file extension"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-16 an empty Language section and an entry without text fail" {
+    glossary ''
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"has no **Term**: entries"* ]]
+    glossary '**Bare**:'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"needs \"**Term**: definition\""* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-17 --json reports the glossary type and its violations" {
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
+    glossary '**Spike**: A prototype.' '**SPIKE**: Again.'
+    run bash -c '"$0" --type glossary --file "$1" --json 2>/dev/null' "$SCRIPT" "$G"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '.type == "glossary" and .pass == false and (.violations | length) == 1' >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "GV-18 an H1 not shaped '# Glossary: <name>' WARNs" {
+    printf '# Words\n\nContext.\n\n## Language\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'WARN:'*'the H1 is not "# Glossary: <name>"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-19 lines inside fenced code in Language are not judged" {
+    glossary '**A**: B.' '' '```' 'not an entry' '_Aliases_: x' '```'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
+# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
+# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
+    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
+    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
+    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
+    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+    git -C "$R" init -q
+    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
+    git -C "$R" config user.name t
+    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
+    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
+    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
+    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
+    commit "base"
+}
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-validator.bats
+#
+# validate-artifact.sh --type glossary (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.4, §4.5): an
+# H1, a context paragraph before '## Language', one-line '**Term**: definition'
+# entries of at most two sentences and 300 characters, _Avoid_: and _Aliases_:
+# only directly below an entry, no duplicate term or alias, WARN on a path or
+# file extension in '## Language'. Cases write temp files only.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+    G="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/GLOSSARY.md"
+}
+
+# glossary <language-section lines...>: a valid head plus the given body
+glossary() {
+    { printf '# Glossary: test\n\nThe vocabulary of a test project.\n\n## Language\n\n'; printf '%s\n' "$@"; } > "$G"
+}
+
+val() { run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$G" "$@"; }
+
+@test "GV-1 the framework glossary validates with no warning" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-2 the root project glossary validates with no warning" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-3 both fixture glossaries validate" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary/ok/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary/miss/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-4 a well-formed entry with _Avoid_ and _Aliases_ lines passes" {
+    glossary '**Dissent**: A second review. It is triaged.' '_Avoid_: second opinion' '_Aliases_: DIS, counter-review' '' '### Group' '' '**Voice**: Who decided.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-5 a duplicate term fails, case-insensitively" {
+    glossary '**Spike**: A prototype.' '' '**spike**: Another one.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'term "spike" duplicates term "Spike"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-6 an alias that repeats a term or another alias fails" {
+    glossary '**Run mode**: Unattended runs.' '_Aliases_: RUNNING' '' '**Halt**: A stop.' '_Aliases_: running, run_mode'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'alias "running" duplicates alias "RUNNING"'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'alias "run_mode" duplicates term "Run mode"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-7 a definition over 300 characters fails" {
+    glossary "**Long**: $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 1 301))."
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'the definition of "Long" is 302 characters, over 300'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-8 a definition of exactly 300 characters passes; multibyte characters count once" {
+    glossary "**Edge**: $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 1 299))." "**Wide**: $(printf 'é%.0s' $(seq 1 299))."
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-9 a three-sentence definition fails; two sentences pass" {
+    glossary '**Three**: One. Two! Three?'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'the definition of "Three" has 3 sentences; at most two'* ]]
+    glossary '**Two**: One sentence here. And a second (with a note).'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-10 _Aliases_ without an entry fails" {
+    glossary '_Aliases_: orphan' '' '**Real**: An entry.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: is not directly after an entry"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-11 _Avoid_ separated from its entry by a blank line fails" {
+    glossary '**Real**: An entry.' '' '_Avoid_: other word'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Avoid_: is not directly after an entry"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-12 a missing ## Language section fails" {
+    printf '# Glossary: test\n\nContext.\n\n## Terms\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'no "## Language" section'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-13 a missing H1 or context paragraph fails" {
+    printf 'Context.\n\n## Language\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no H1"* ]]
+    printf '# Glossary: test\n\n## Language\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no context paragraph"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-14 a definition wrapped onto a second line fails" {
+    glossary '**Wrapped**: A definition that' 'continues on the next line.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"not an entry"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-15 a path or file extension in a definition WARNs and still passes" {
+    glossary '**Hook**: The guard in hooks/implement-gate that asks first.' '**Doc**: The plan in a markdown file named plan.md for review.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *":7: a path or file extension"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *":8: a path or file extension"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-16 an empty Language section and an entry without text fail" {
+    glossary ''
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"has no **Term**: entries"* ]]
+    glossary '**Bare**:'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"needs \"**Term**: definition\""* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-17 --json reports the glossary type and its violations" {
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
+    glossary '**Spike**: A prototype.' '**SPIKE**: Again.'
+    run bash -c '"$0" --type glossary --file "$1" --json 2>/dev/null' "$SCRIPT" "$G"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '.type == "glossary" and .pass == false and (.violations | length) == 1' >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "GV-18 an H1 not shaped '# Glossary: <name>' WARNs" {
+    printf '# Words\n\nContext.\n\n## Language\n\n**A**: B.\n' > "$G"
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'WARN:'*'the H1 is not "# Glossary: <name>"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-19 lines inside fenced code in Language are not judged" {
+    glossary '**A**: B.' '' '```' 'not an entry' '_Aliases_: x' '```'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
+# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
+# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
+    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
+    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
+    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
+    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+    git -C "$R" init -q
+    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
+    git -C "$R" config user.name t
+    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
+    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
+    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
+    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
+    commit "base"
+}
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-terms.bats
+#
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, §5.3) keeps every
+# backticked span of the kernel that matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ outside
+# fenced code and fails unless each one resolves to a glossary **Term**, an
+# _Aliases_: token (case-insensitive, plural s/es folded) or an allowlist line
+# (at most 30). Every case below works on temp copies; the live kernel,
+# glossary and allowlist are only ever read.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh"
+    KERNEL="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    GLOSSARY="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    ALLOW="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary"
+    W="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    printf '# Glossary: t\nTest vocabulary.\n\n## Language\n\n**Widget**: A thing.\n\n**Run mode**: Unattended runs.\n_Aliases_: RUNNING, JACKED_OUT\n\n**Box**: A container.\n' > "$W/g.md"
+    printf '# test allowlist\nparse_it   # code identifier\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+}
+
+# check <kernel text>: run the checker on a temp kernel with the temp glossary and allowlist
+check() {
+    printf '%s\n' "$1" > "$W/k.md"
+    shift
+    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$W/k.md" --glossary "$W/g.md" --allowlist "$W/a.txt" "$@"
+}
+
+@test "GT-1 the live kernel, framework glossary and allowlist pass" {
+    run "$CHECK"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 0"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-2 removing a term from a copy of the glossary fails and names the token" {
+    grep -v '^_Aliases_: br$' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
+    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `br`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"define **br**"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: line"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist it in"* ]]

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-terms.bats
+#
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, §5.3) keeps every
+# backticked span of the kernel that matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ outside
+# fenced code and fails unless each one resolves to a glossary **Term**, an
+# _Aliases_: token (case-insensitive, plural s/es folded) or an allowlist line
+# (at most 30). Every case below works on temp copies; the live kernel,
+# glossary and allowlist are only ever read.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh"
+    KERNEL="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    GLOSSARY="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    ALLOW="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary"
+    W="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    printf '# Glossary: t\nTest vocabulary.\n\n## Language\n\n**Widget**: A thing.\n\n**Run mode**: Unattended runs.\n_Aliases_: RUNNING, JACKED_OUT\n\n**Box**: A container.\n' > "$W/g.md"
+    printf '# test allowlist\nparse_it   # code identifier\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+}
+
+# check <kernel text>: run the checker on a temp kernel with the temp glossary and allowlist
+check() {
+    printf '%s\n' "$1" > "$W/k.md"
+    shift
+    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$W/k.md" --glossary "$W/g.md" --allowlist "$W/a.txt" "$@"
+}
+
+@test "GT-1 the live kernel, framework glossary and allowlist pass" {
+    run "$CHECK"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 0"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-2 removing a term from a copy of the glossary fails and names the token" {
+    grep -v '^_Aliases_: br$' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
+    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `br`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"define **br**"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: line"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist it in"* ]]

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# validate-artifact.sh --type sprint: the '### Seams Under Test' rule gated on the plan's
+# header **Date:** (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.2; SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-13).
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+    T="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}"
+}
+
+# A plan with two sprint blocks; $1 = header date line (may be empty), $2 = seams in sprint 1
+# (yes|no|empty), $3 = seams in sprint 2 (yes|no|empty).
+seams_block() {
+    case "$1" in
+        yes) printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n| `tool.sh` exit code | a wrong exit | prose | new |\n\n' ;;
+        empty) printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n\n' ;;
+        *) ;;
+    esac
+}
+sprint_body() {
+    printf '### Sprint Goal\ng\n\n### Deliverables\n- [ ] d\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] c\n\n'
+    printf '### Technical Tasks\n- [ ] Task %s → **[G-1]**\n\n' "$2"
+    seams_block "$1"
+    printf '### Dependencies\n- none\n\n### Security Considerations\n- none\n\n'
+    printf '### Risks & Mitigation\n| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| r | Low | Low | m |\n\n'
+    printf '### Success Metrics\n- m\n\n'
+}
+plan() {
+    printf '# Sprint Plan: x\n\n**Version:** 1.0\n'
+    [[ -n "$1" ]] && printf '**Date:** %s\n' "$1"
+    printf '**Author:** test\n\n---\n\n'
+    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2" "1.1"

input.command: cd /workspace; sed -n 1900,2194p pr/head.diff
input.description: Read diff lines 1900 to end

content.content:
+    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2" "1.1"
+    printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up\n\n'; sprint_body "$3" "2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation"
+    printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-1 a plan dated 2026-10-13 without the block fails and names each sprint missing it" {
+    plan 2026-10-13 yes no > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up (line"*"has no '### Seams Under Test' table"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"Sprint 1: Foundation (line"*"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-2 the same plan with the block in every sprint passes without a seams WARN" {
+    plan 2026-10-13 yes yes > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" != *"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-3 a later date also requires it; a heading with no table row counts as missing" {
+    plan 2026-11-02 empty yes > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Sprint 1: Foundation (line"*"has no '### Seams Under Test' table with at least one row"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-4 a plan dated 2026-10-12 without the block passes with one WARN" {
+    plan 2026-10-12 no no > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: 2026-10-12 plan: 2 sprint block(s) without a '### Seams Under Test' table"* ]]
+    [ "$(grep -c 'Seams Under Test' <<< "$output")" -eq 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-5 an undated plan passes with one WARN" {
+    plan "" no no > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: undated plan: 2 sprint block(s)"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-6 a Date line below the first H2 is not the header date (the plan reads as undated)" {
+    { plan "" no no; printf '\n## Notes\n\n**Date:** 2026-12-01\n'; } > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: undated plan"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-7 a Seams heading inside fenced code does not count; a block under a later H2 does not either" {
+    {
+        plan 2026-10-13 yes no | sed '/^## Appendix/,$d'
+        printf '```\n### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| a | b | c | d |\n```\n\n'
+        printf '## Risk Register\n\n### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| a | b | c | d |\n\n'
+        printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
+    } > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up (line"*"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-8 this cycle's grimoires/loa/sprint.md passes" {
+    [ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ] || skip "no live sprint plan in this checkout"
+    grep -q '^\*\*Date:\*\* 2026-10-1[3-9]' "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" || skip "the live plan is not the cycle-128 plan"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" != *"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-9 the archived cycle-127 plan (dated 2026-10-07) gains only a WARN from the rule" {
+    local f="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/sprint-seams/cycle-127-sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$f"
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: 2026-10-07 plan: 1 sprint block(s) without a '### Seams Under Test' table"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"has no '### Seams Under Test' table with"* ]]
+    # The plan predates the template's Risks & Mitigation / Success Metrics sections and fails
+    # on those alone, exactly as it did before the seams rule; the rule adds no violation.
+    local others
+    others="$(grep -v '^WARN\|^INFO' <<< "$output" | grep -vc "missing required section '### \(Risks & Mitigation\|Success Metrics\)'" || true)"
+    [ "$others" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-10 the shipped sprint template carries the block in each full sprint block" {
+    local t="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md"
+    [ "$(grep -c '^### Seams Under Test$' "$t")" -eq 2 ]
+    [ "$(grep -c '^| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |$' "$t")" -eq 2 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
+# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
+#
+# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
+# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
+# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
+# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
+# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
+# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
+# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
+# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
+# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
+# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
+#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
+#
+#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
+#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
+#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
+#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
+#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
+#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
+#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
+JSON=0
+REPORT=0
+ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
+
+need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
+  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
+fi
+
+# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
+rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
+DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+
+# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  {
+    s = $0
+    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
+      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
+      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
+    }
+  }
+' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
+
+# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
+#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
+  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
+  !lang { next }
+  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
+    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
+    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
+    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
+  }
+  /^_Aliases_:/ {
+    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
+    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
+    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
+      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
+      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
+    }
+  }
+' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
+
+# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
+awk '
+  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
+    if (s == "") next
+    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
+' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
+
+# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
+#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
+#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
+#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
+#    glossary already resolves.
+awk -F'\t' '
+  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
+  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
+  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
+  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
+  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
+                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
+                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
+  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
+  {
+    used[norm($2)] = 1
+    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
+    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
+    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
+    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
+    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
+  }
+  END {
+    for (k in allow) {
+      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
+      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
+        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
+    }
+  }
+' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+
+kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
+n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
+
+violations=()
+warnings=()
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
+  case "$r" in
+    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
+    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
+    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
+  esac
+done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
+  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
+fi
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
+     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
+     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
+     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
+    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
+    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
+    | {ok: null,
+       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
+       kept: ($tokens | length),
+       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
+                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
+                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
+                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
+       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
+       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
+       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
+       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
+       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
+       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
+       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
+    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
+  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+else
+  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
+      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+  fi
+  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
+  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
+  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
+  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
+fi
+
+[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
+exit 0

tool_use_result.stdout:
+    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2" "1.1"
+    printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up\n\n'; sprint_body "$3" "2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation"
+    printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
+# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
+#
+# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
+# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
+# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
+# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
+# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
+# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
+# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
+# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
+# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
+# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
+#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
+#
+#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
+#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
+#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
+#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
+#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
+#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
+#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
+JSON=0
+REPORT=0
+ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
+
+need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
+  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
+fi
+
+# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
+rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
+DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+
+# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  {
+    s = $0
+    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
+      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
+      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
+    }
+  }
+' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
+
+# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
+#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
+  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
+  !lang { next }
+  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
+    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
+    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
+    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
+  }
+  /^_Aliases_:/ {
+    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
+    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
+    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
+      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
+      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
+    }
+  }
+' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
+
+# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
+awk '
+  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
+    if (s == "") next
+    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
+' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
+
+# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
+#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
+#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
+#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
+#    glossary already resolves.
+awk -F'\t' '
+  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
+  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
+  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
+  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
+  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
+                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
+                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
+  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
+  {
+    used[norm($2)] = 1
+    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
+    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
+    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
+    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
+    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
+  }
+  END {
+    for (k in allow) {
+      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
+      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
+        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
+    }
+  }
+' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+
+kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
+n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
+
+violations=()
+warnings=()
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
+  case "$r" in
+    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
+    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
+    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
+  esac
+done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
+  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
+fi
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
+     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
+     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
+     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
+    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
+    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
+    | {ok: null,
+       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
+       kept: ($tokens | length),
+       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
+                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
+                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
+                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
+       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
+       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
+       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
+       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
+       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
+       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
+       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
+    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
+  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+else
+  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
+      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+  fi
+  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
+  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
+  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
+  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
+fi
+
+[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
+exit 0

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (PR: cycle-128 sprint-254 glossaries, seams, red-before-green)

Phase 2 notes to seed the dissent. Scope: pr/head.diff (29 files).

1. reviewing-code/SKILL.md grants `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` under `deny_raw_shell: true`. The script runs any argv after `--` (and `--setup <cmd>`), so the review skill gains an arbitrary-command path; Phase 2 text takes the Red commit from reviewer.md (the implementer's report) and does not say where the test command comes from.
2. red-test-check.sh symlinks live-tree dependency dirs (node_modules .venv vendor target .tox) into the worktrees by default, so `--setup` (e.g. a package install) and tests write into the live tree's copies; the bats header claims the live tree is never touched.

8. .claude/checksums.json not regenerated although .claude/ files changed (verify whether the repo requires it per PR).

EOF

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** ${D}
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= pr/PR.md)
**Change under review:** pr/head.diff — "feat(cycle-128): sprint-254 decision surfaces, part 3 — glossaries, seams under test, red-before-green" (29 files)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change delivers three coherent pieces: a framework glossary with a kernel-term drift gate (\`tools/check-glossary-terms.sh\`, CI workflow, fixtures), a \`### Seams Under Test\` rule in the sprint validator plus a \`--type glossary\` validator, and \`red-test-check.sh\`, a worktree-based red-before-green checker wired into the bug micro-sprint template and the review skill. The shell is careful (argument-injection guards, process-group kill, cleanup on every exit path, pipefail-safe greps) and the four new bats suites are substantive. I executed all four suites against the head tree: 66 tests, 0 failures, 1 skip (SEAMS-8, no cycle-128 plan in this checkout). The \`pr/head/\` bundle had lost the executable bit the diff declares (\`new file mode 100755\`); restoring it was the only setup needed, so that is a bundle artifact, not a PR defect.

One finding blocks: the review skill, which declares \`deny_raw_shell: true\` and allowlists a handful of fixed scripts, now allowlists a script whose job is to execute any argv (and any \`--setup\` argv) in two worktrees with the live tree's dependency directories symlinked in, and the skill text sources the inputs from the implementer's own report. That widens a process fence the framework relies on, in the gate meant to check the implementer. The rest are non-blocking: live-tree writes through the linked dependency directories (demonstrated), a missing CHANGELOG entry, unregenerated checksums, and a handful of validator and glossary edge cases.

Adversarial cross-model review (Phase 2.5) did not produce findings: the run stopped at its own cost estimate (\`status: budget_exceeded\`, 214c over the configured 200c for two voices) before any model call; the failure is recorded in \`adversarial-review.json\` via \`--record-fallback\`. This is a single-model assessment.

Karpathy pass: the implementation is lean for what it does. Lean already. Ship (after the fix below).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security / Process fence — the review skill gains an arbitrary-command path fed from the implementer's report

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) \`head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219\` — the review skill is told to run \`red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> -- <test command>\`; the Red commit comes from the implementer's report and the test command's source is unspecified, so the party under review chooses the argv the reviewer executes.
**File:** \`head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6\`, \`:27\`, \`:39\`, \`:219\`; \`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:288-306\` (\`--setup\` argv), \`:222-227\` (dependency symlinks into the live tree)
**Issue:** The skill declares \`deny_raw_shell: true\` (line 39) and its Bash allowlist is a short list of fixed framework scripts. Line 6 and line 27 add \`Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)\`. That script runs whatever follows \`--\` (and whatever \`--setup\` names) as a process in each worktree; nothing in the skill or the script constrains that argv. Phase 2 (line 219) takes the red SHA from \`reviewer.md\`, which the implementer writes, and says nothing about where the test command comes from — in practice it will be copied from the same report. The red worktree is a checkout of the implementer's commit, and \`link_deps\` (lines 222-227) symlinks the live tree's \`node_modules .venv vendor target .tox\` into it, so the executed argv can write into the reviewer's live tree (verified: a \`--setup "touch node_modules/x"\` and a test writing \`node_modules/y\` both landed in the live tree's directory).
**Why This Matters:** The review gate exists to check the implementer's work independently; the framework enforces that with tool fences ("disallowed-tools strips write tools from pure-review skills", \`deny_raw_shell\`). This change gives the reviewer an unconstrained exec path and lets the implementer's report dictate what runs through it. A compromised or prompt-injected implementation turn can thereby run code under the reviewer's identity and modify the reviewer's live environment. CWE-78 (OS command injection via untrusted input) / CWE-829 (inclusion of functionality from an untrusted control sphere); OWASP ASVS V5 (input validation at trust boundaries).
**Required Fix:**
1. In \`SKILL.md\` Phase 2, name the trusted source of the test command: the sprint plan's test command (e.g. a \`red_test.command\` field in sprint.md / the micro-sprint template), explicitly "never from \`reviewer.md\`"; keep only the SHA from the report and have the script validate it (it already does).
2. Narrow the allowlist pattern to the shape the skill needs, e.g. \`Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red *)\`, and have the review invocation pass \`--no-link-deps\` (or make linking opt-in via \`--link-deps\`) and omit \`--setup\`, so a review-time run cannot write into the live tree.
3. Update \`micro-sprint.md:43\` and RTC-17 (which pins the current wording) to match.
**Reference:** CWE-78, CWE-829; \`.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\` "Process Compliance" (fence stack), \`reviewing-code/SKILL.md:39\` \`deny_raw_shell: true\`.

---

## Observations

### 1. red-test-check.sh — the live tree is written through the linked dependency directories

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) \`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:227\` — \`ln -s "\${MAIN}/\${d}" "\${wt}/\${d}"\` makes every write a \`--setup\` or test makes under \`node_modules\`, \`.venv\`, \`vendor\`, \`target\` or \`.tox\` land in the live tree; \`--setup "npm ci"\` at the red commit rewrites the live install to the old lockfile.
**File:** \`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:47\`, \`:222-227\`, \`:288-306\`; \`head/tests/unit/red-test-check.bats:3-4\`
**Suggestion:** Line 29 documents the hazard for tests, but the common case is \`--setup\` (package install) and the bats header (lines 3-4) claims "the live tree was not touched", which no test checks for these directories. Either copy-on-write the dependency directories (e.g. \`cp -al\` / reflink where available), make linking opt-in, or at least refuse \`--setup\` while deps are linked, and add a test that asserts the live dependency directory is unchanged after a run. Verified with a fixture: files created by \`--setup\` and by the test appeared in the live \`node_modules\`.
**Benefit:** Keeps the script's own invariant ("nothing in the live tree is touched") true for the default invocation.

### 2. Documentation — no CHANGELOG entry

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) \`head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:1\` — a new CI gate, a new validator type, a new review-time script and two glossaries ship with no \`CHANGELOG.md\` \`[Unreleased]\` entry in the diff.
**File:** \`head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:1\`, \`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:1\`, \`head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:1\`
**Suggestion:** Add the \`[Unreleased]\` entries (the repository convention, see the cycle-127 fixture's own task list). If the cycle lands the CHANGELOG in its final PR, say so in the PR description.
**Benefit:** The documentation-verification gate treats a missing CHANGELOG entry per task as blocking; stating the plan avoids a round-trip at audit.

### 3. Integrity — System Zone files changed without regenerating checksums.json

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: low) \`head/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md:1\` — three new and seven modified \`.claude/\` files, no \`.claude/checksums.json\` update in the diff; \`check-loa.sh\` verifies mounted files against it and \`integrity_enforcement: strict\` halts on drift.
**File:** \`head/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md:1\`, \`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1\`, \`head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:1\`
**Suggestion:** If the repository regenerates checksums at release time only, no action; otherwise run the generator (\`mount-loa.sh generate_checksums\` / \`ground-truth-gen.sh\`) in this PR. Low confidence because the convention is not visible from the PR bundle.
**Benefit:** Avoids a false integrity halt in consumer projects that mount this commit.

### 4. Glossary validator — abbreviations count as sentence ends

- **LOW** (confidence: high) \`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1297\` — \`gsub(/[.!?]+[)"]*[[:space:]]/, ...)\` counts "e.g. " / "i.e. " / "v1. " as sentence boundaries; a two-sentence definition containing "e.g." is rejected as three sentences (reproduced).
**Suggestion:** Skip a boundary when the preceding token is a known abbreviation or a single letter, or make the sentence rule a WARN.

### 5. Seams rule — a template placeholder row satisfies it; an indented table does not

- **LOW** (confidence: high) \`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:884-885\` — any \`|\`-prefixed line after the separator counts as a row, so the unfilled template row \`| {interface the tests drive} | ... |\` (\`head/.claude/skills/planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md:65\`) passes; conversely a table indented by 1-3 spaces (legal Markdown) is not matched by \`/^\\|/\` and the sprint reads as missing the block.
**Suggestion:** Reject rows whose cells are all \`{...}\` placeholders; allow \`^[[:space:]]{0,3}\\|\`.

### 6. Seams rule — the date gate is advisory in practice

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) \`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:871\`, \`:897\` — a plan without a header \`**Date:**\` only WARNs, so omitting the date opts out of the rule. Acceptable for the migration, but the WARN should name that it is the reason the rule did not apply, and the planning skill should require the date.

### 7. red-test-check.sh — the green run happens before the red verdict is applied

- **LOW** (confidence: high) \`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:308-318\` — both runs execute before the red-side checks at line 318, so a red TIMEOUT or DECOY still pays for the full green run (reproduced: \`--timeout 2\` with a slow red took 4 s). Decide the red side first and skip green when it is already TIMEOUT/DECOY/NOT_A_RED; the header's "judged first" then matches the control flow.

### 8. red-test-check.sh — broad not-a-red patterns

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) \`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:65\`, \`:69\` — \`'SyntaxError'\` and \`'build failed'\` match legitimate assertion output (a parser test printing the SyntaxError it expected; a message containing "build failed"), turning a real red into NOT_A_RED. The header calls this out as a heuristic the reviewer may overrule; anchoring the node pattern (\`^SyntaxError:\` / \`^\\s+SyntaxError\`) and the go one (\`^FAIL.*\\[build failed\\]\`) would cut the false negatives.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) \`head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:105\` — \`entry\` is empty for an \`_Aliases_:\` line that precedes the first term, the lookup returns "" and the token reads MISS (reproduced). The validator rejects such a file, so the impact is a confusing message; print the alias's own name as the entry or skip the line with a WARN. The first two exist to satisfy the kernel gate; consider separate entries ("Run state", "Jack out") and widen the Flatline definition.

### 11. Mount manifest — no test for the new GLOSSARY.md entry

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) \`head/.claude/scripts/lib/symlink-manifest.sh:79\` — the sibling entries have a manifest test (\`test-mount-submodule-default.bats\` "manifest includes feedback-ontology.yaml"); the new entry has none, so a future edit that drops it goes unnoticed.

- Read the full 29-file diff, then rebuilt the head tree on an executable filesystem and ran all four new bats suites. Result: 66 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip. The `pr/head/` bundle had dropped the executable bit the diff declares, which is a bundle artifact, not a PR defect.
